{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line (stroke 2), the entire lower outline of the fish, and it carries from the start all the way to the tail. That lower contour is half of what makes the fish read as a fish, and by eye about 109 of 110 dominoes fall from the start. I also cleared the stray dominoes under the top line by the dip, so nothing loose sat in the picture.

Execution: I laid the belly in several steady batches of 5-7 dominoes, tracing it from the line near the nose so it branched off gently and joined the run correctly. I then inspected the area closely twice to confirm the chain was continuous, and removed the strays without disturbing the top line. When the build was done I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed with short status updates (belly done and connected, strays cleared, hands off) so others could plan the tail join and final checks without guessing. I left the tail join to Sofia and Jack to avoid doubling up on dominoes, and I helped keep the mood light and focused through the final minutes.

Leadership: I helped the table stay calm and disciplined at the end by calling for hands off early and modelling it myself, which protected the finished picture. I kept energy up with a good-humoured tone and made sure the status of my section was always clear to everyone.

Overall, the fish is a clear, recognizable animal outline, and my belly line and clean-up were a solid part of getting there.", "my_share_percent": 30}
